title: Minimum Operations to Halve Array Sum
summary: Given an array of positive integers, you need to determine the minimum number of operations required to reduce the sum of the array by at least half.
statement: Given an array of positive integers, you need to determine the minimum number of operations required to reduce the sum of the array by at least half. In each operation, you can select any number from the array and replace it with its half.
constraints: One operation replaces one current value by exactly half of itself.
Continue until the array sum has decreased by at least half of its original value.
Return the minimum operation count; intermediate values may be fractional.
reference_solution:
def minimum_halving_operations(nums):
    import heapq
    heap=[-float(value) for value in nums];heapq.heapify(heap)
    target=sum(nums)/2;reduced=0;operations=0
    while reduced<target:
        largest=-heapq.heappop(heap);half=largest/2
        reduced+=half;operations+=1;heapq.heappush(heap,-half)
    return operations

hints: Each operation gains half of the value selected, so the largest current value gives the greatest immediate reduction.
Use a max-heap and track accumulated reduction against half the original sum.
Pop the largest, add its half to reduced, push that half back, and count until the target is reached.
An exchange argument replaces any smaller choice with the current largest without reducing progress, so the greedy sequence minimizes operations.

tests.explanation: Halving the current largest value at each step reaches half the original sum in three operations.
Halving twenty, then ten, reduces at least half of the original total in two operations.
